title: POC weekly sync - rollout & go-live planning
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on rollout planning: canary strategy, A/B options, monitoring dashboards, runbook ownership and rollback criteria. Agreed next steps for runbook review, canary schedule on staging, and security doc exchange.
next_steps: Redwood to share canary runbook template and example metrics dashboard by 2026-09-18
Acme to confirm cutover target week (tentatively 2026-10-04) by 2026-09-20
Danny to run staging canary and share results (latency, error rate) by 2026-09-22
Laura to validate SSO/SAML and KMS integration plan with security team by 2026-09-21
action_items: Danny Cho (Redwood SE) - prepare staging canary run and collect p95/p99 latency + error rate (due: 2026-09-22)
Sara Mitchell (Redwood AE) - send pricing sheet + Dedicated capacity options and draft runbook template (due: 2026-09-18)
Raj Patel (Acme) - confirm stakeholder list and final cutover week (due: 2026-09-20)
Laura Gomez (Acme) - coordinate SSO/KMS contacts and share any policy blockers (due: 2026-09-21)
Mike Chen (Acme SRE) - create initial monitoring dashboard in Grafana with p50/p95/p99 and request tracing hooks (due: 2026-09-24)
transcript:
[00:00] Sara (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we have 45 minutes so we'll focus on the canary/cutover details and next steps. quick roll call?
[00:08] Raj (Customer): Raj here, Laura, Mike on as well.
[00:12] Laura (Customer): hi all.
[00:15] Danny (Redwood SE): Danny here - I'll cover the technical plan for the canary.
[00:20] Sara (Redwood): ok great. quick recap: last week we validated inference quality on your sample traffic and ran the 50k token eval. results looked good but there was a slight p99 latency bump under bursty load, Danny did a follow up tune.
[00:35] Danny (Redwood SE): yeah so the p50/p95 are solid, p99 spiked when KV cache misses aligned with long context requests. i adjusted batching window and we re-ran with aggressive prefix caching. improvement was ~18% on p99 in staging but we need a real canary on production traffic shape to be comfortable.
[01:05] Raj (Customer): can you explain the canary approach you're recommending? we have compliance concerns so we want a phased rollout.
[01:12] Danny (Redwood SE): recommended two-phase: stage canary first (1% traffic, mirrored requests to Redwood hosted endpoint), measure latency, errors, and semantic regression using a small eval set. then a canary in production with traffic shift 1->5->20% over a week depending on metrics. alternate is A/B where both variants serve and we compare outputs, but that requires dual writing and more infra.
[01:38] Laura (Customer): our preference is canary to start, simpler for audit trail. what metrics do you need?
[01:42] Danny (Redwood SE): key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec throughput, error rate (5xx/timeout), semantic regression score on the baseline prompt set, and cost delta per 1000 requests. also route-level tracing and request IDs to link to our logs.
[02:05] Mike (Customer SRE): for rollback criteria we want clear thresholds. if p99 > 1.5x baseline or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes, we auto-roll back. are those thresholds realistic?
[02:18] Sara (Redwood AE): that seems reasonable as a starting point. we usually recommend p99 target aligned to your SLA; what is your internal SLA?
[02:25] Raj (Customer): for this feature we commit to < 800ms p95, but p99 we only have internal target of 1.2s. so 1.5x of current feels ok as rollback.
[02:36] Danny (Redwood SE): ok we'll set the canary gating so if p99 exceeds 1.2s * 1.5 or error rate > 0.5% we stop the rollout and rollback. we'll also add semantic fidelity checks - if the regression on the sample prompt set crosses threshold (we'll propose 3% drop in score) we stop.
[02:58] Laura (Customer): and monitoring? we use Grafana/Prometheus and Datadog for traces. can you push metrics there or do we pull from Redwood?
[03:07] Danny (Redwood SE): Redwood exposes Prometheus metrics and we can push a metrics endpoint; we also provide a JSON webhook for alerts. for traces we can add headers to span request IDs so it correlates with your APM.
[03:20] Sara (Redwood AE): note: we'll share a sample dashboard. Danny will include the exact metric names and tags so your SREs can wire up alerts.
[03:28] Mike (Customer SRE): we need RBAC and audit logs for all admin actions (model roll, config change). is that available in Private / Dedicated?
[03:36] Danny (Redwood SE): yes Dedicated and Private both have audit logs, RBAC and KMS integration. for hosted routes we have admin audit trails in the console, and we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or cloud watch. small caveat: hosted audit retention is 90 days by default unless you add the compliance add-on.
[03:56] Raj (Customer): security team will want SOC2 artifacts and encryption at rest details. will you send the security pack?
[04:02] Sara (Redwood AE): yes we'll share our security pack and SOC2 AOC. i'll include KMS integration notes and sample compliance matrix.
[04:10] Danny (Redwood SE): back to cutover: for the canary we suggest a staging dress rehearsal on 9/20 with synthetic traffic shaped to mimic peak patterns, then production canary starting 9/27 if staging is green. does that timeline work?
[04:25] Raj (Customer): tentative yes, but i need to confirm with product ops and security.
[04:30] Laura (Customer): is there a cost delta for canaries? do we pay full token costs for mirrored requests?
[04:36] Sara (Redwood AE): mirrored requests count toward usage; for a short staging run we can offer to absorb some of the cost but production traffic will be billed. i'll include cost estimates for 1%, 5%, 20% traffic scenarios.
[04:49] Mike (Customer SRE): uptime and fallback: if Redwood endpoint degrades can we fail back to our legacy model?
[04:55] Danny (Redwood SE): yes, smart routing supports automatic fallback to a pinned fallback model or region. we can configure a policy: if latency > threshold for X minutes, traffic routes back. we'll document the policy and test it in the dress rehearsal.
[05:10] Raj (Customer): i want to be explicit about runbook owners — who will be oncall during the canary and who triggers rollbacks?
[05:18] Sara (Redwood AE): proposal: Acme SRE owns immediate rollback trigger in production, Redwood SE acts as secondary to assist with triage. Redwood will be on 24/7 on-call during initial ramp if you choose the paid pilot support add-on.
[05:32] Laura (Customer): for audit we need the runbook steps in writing, including who approves the cutover.
[05:38] Danny (Redwood SE): i'll draft a runbook template with specific commands for rollback, how to validate semantic regression, and playbook for contacting Redwood support.
[05:46] Sara (Redwood AE): good. on A/B vs canary, any reason to choose A/B now?
[05:51] Raj (Customer): A/B is nice for side-by-side quality comparison but it's heavier on infra and data capture. for first rollout we prefer canary.
[05:59] Danny (Redwood SE): agreed. canary gives lower blast radius and easier auditing. we can run an A/B for feature gating later if you want deeper model comparison.
[06:10] Mike (Customer SRE): logging format — request IDs and user IDs: we need PII redaction. will Redwood strip user PII before logs leave our VPC?
[06:19] Danny (Redwood SE): if you go Dedicated or Private you control ingress and we can ensure PII doesn't leave your network. for hosted we support client-side tokenization or field-level redaction. we'll document options.
[06:32] Laura (Customer): ok. next: notifications and SLO alerting — we want Slack + PagerDuty integration for canary alerts.
[06:39] Sara (Redwood AE): Redwood supports webhook, Slack, and PagerDuty. we'll include example alerting rules and a suggested runbook mapping to PagerDuty escalations.
[06:49] Raj (Customer): is there any manual step required for cutover that might block an automated rollout? e.g., approvals, DB migrations?
[06:55] Danny (Redwood SE): nothing on Redwood's side, but if your product needs a schema or feature flag flip we should include that in the runbook. we can gate the rollout on an external webhook that only fires after your approval.
[07:06] Sara (Redwood AE): ok let's summarize decisions: canary approach, staging dress rehearsal 9/20, prod canary target 9/27, rollback thresholds p99 > 1.8s or error rate > 0.5% sustained 10m, Redwood to provide runbook and dashboards. action owners as discussed.
[07:25] Raj (Customer): sounds good. can you also provide an example of the canary traffic config (weights and duration)?
[07:31] Danny (Redwood SE): yes example: 1% for 2 hours, review metrics; if green move to 5% for 4 hours, then 20% for 24 hours, then 100% over 48 hours. but we can tailor durations.
[07:46] Laura (Customer): what about data retention for logs? compliance requires 1 year for audit trails.
[07:51] Sara (Redwood AE): hosted default is 90 days, with paid retention add-on for 1 year. Dedicated/Private you can retain per your policy. i'll include retention options in the security pack.
[08:02] Mike (Customer SRE): who will run the final cutover? we need a runbook approval meeting.
[08:07] Sara (Redwood AE): i propose a cutover readiness meeting a week before the target with both engineering leads and security. we'll schedule once cutover week is confirmed.
[08:17] Raj (Customer): ok i'll try to confirm 9/27 cutover by next Monday.
[08:21] Danny (Redwood SE): i'll start the staging canary tests and share the run results in the slack channel.
[08:26] Sara (Redwood AE): i'll send the pricing + security docs and the canary/runbook templates today.
[08:30] Raj (Customer): thanks all. any other questions?
[08:33] Laura (Customer): can you include a brief checklist for security review? our team wants to see items like encryption, KMS, SAML, retention, audit exports.
[08:40] Sara (Redwood AE): yes will attach the compliance checklist.
[08:43] Mike (Customer SRE): one small thing — is there an SLA option for p99? we usually contract p95 but want p99 visibility.
[08:50] Sara (Redwood AE): we can provide SLOs for p99 in the Dedicated contract as a custom SLA. i'll note that as a negotiation point.
[08:58] Raj (Customer): great, thanks everyone.
[09:00] Sara (Redwood AE): thanks, we'll follow up with the items discussed. meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript contains typical auto-transcribe artifacts and occasional overlaps; names sometimes truncated. References to artifacts: "canary runbook template" (link: /redwood/docs/canary-runbook), "security pack" (link: /redwood/security/soc2-pack.pdf), and sample dashboard (link: /redwood/dashboards/acme-canary.json).
